book_title: Nine Yard Sarees: A Short Story Cycle
subject_line: The scattered family in Nine Yard Sarees
email_body:
Dear Prasanthi,

Nine Yard Sarees follows several generations of a Tamil Brahmin family dispersed across Singapore, Australia and the United States, and I was struck by your choice of a short story cycle rather than a single novel to hold them together.

I would love to ask how you decided which family members got their own stories, and what the cycle form let you do with distance between them.

subject_line: Lockdown poems in Anatomy of a Wave
email_body:
Dear Shu Hoong,

In your Tatler Asia interview you described the worst lockdowns as becoming a kind of writing residency, and many of the poems from that time ended up in Anatomy of a Wave, which brought you a third Singapore Literature Prize.

I would like to ask what that enforced stillness changed in how you wrote, and whether the wave of the title came before or after those poems.

email_body:

subject_line: Doris's last request in Patrick Zhou
email_body:
Dear Ally,

The Disappearance of Patrick Zhou opens on a striking request: Doris, in her last lucid moments, asks her granddaughter Layla to find out what happened to an uncle who vanished on his way to a conference.

As a poet as well as a novelist, how did you approach a mystery built around family memory, and did you know what had happened to Patrick before you started writing?

subject_line: 44 old poems and 44 new in ownself say ownself
email_body:

I would love to ask how you chose what to salvage, and what putting the old poems next to the new ones showed you about your own writing since sonnets from the singlish.

email_body:
عزيزتي ريم،

لفتني في «يوميات روز» أنها تعود إلى حيّ الشندغة في دبي خلال ستينيات القرن الماضي، قبل قيام الدولة، وأنها كانت أول رواية إماراتية تصل إلى القائمة القصيرة للجائزة العالمية للرواية العربية، ثم صدرت بالإنجليزية بترجمة تشيب روسيتي. وقد قرأت أيضاً عن وصولك إلى القائمة القصيرة لجائزة أدب البريكس 2025.

أودّ أن أسألك: كيف بنيتِ صوت روز من داخل حيّ لم يعد قائماً بالشكل الذي تصفينه، وما الذي تغيّر في نظرتك إليه حين قرأتِه بلغة أخرى؟

«دفتر المؤلف» (The Author Ledger) مشروع مستقل يقدّم لمحات قصيرة عن الكتّاب. تُبنى اللمحة عبر بضعة أسئلة مكتوبة تجيبين عنها على مهل، ويُرسل إليك النص الكامل لمراجعته قبل النشر.

هل تودّين المشاركة؟ لا حرج إطلاقاً في أي جواب.

مع خالص التحية،
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Rose's Diary set in Shindagha, Dubai in the 1960s; first Emirati novel on IPAF shortlist (2022); English translation by Chip Rossetti; 2025 BRICS Literature Award shortlist (arabicfiction.org, arablit, esgmena via search results). Residence not verified, so state/city left blank.

subject_line: The Creek elders in House to House
email_body:

I was struck by how House to House grew out of a year and a half of conversations with elders and long-time residents around Dubai Creek, and how your family's photographs from the 1940s to the 1980s fed into the three volumes of poems.

I'd love to ask how you moved from an interview transcript to a poem: what did you keep of a person's own phrasing, and what did you let go?

email_body:
عزيزتي نادية،

توقفت عند فكرة «ملمس الضوء»: نورة الفاقدة للبصر تتعرّف إلى صور فوتوغرافية عبر تطبيق يشرح محتواها، ومن خلالها تستعيد الرواية دبي والإمارات قبل النفط، معتمدةً على الحواس الأخرى. وقد وصلت الرواية إلى القائمة القصيرة للجائزة العالمية للرواية العربية 2025، وفازت بجائزة أفضل كتاب إماراتي (رواية) في معرض الشارقة الدولي للكتاب 2025.

سؤالي: كيف كتبتِ مشاهد تُرى بالصوت واللمس لا بالعين، وهل غيّر ذلك طريقتك في الوصف؟

مع خالص التحية،
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Texture of Light: blind protagonist Noura reads photos via an app; evokes pre-oil Dubai; IPAF 2025 shortlist; SIBF 2025 Best Emirati Book (Novel) (WAM, Khaleej Times, Sharjah24 via search results). Residence not verified.

email_body:

subject_line: The absurd scenarios in Anything but Human
email_body:

I'd like to ask how you decide when an absurd premise should stay playful and when it should turn serious, and whether your work as a translator shapes that instinct.

subject_line: 关于《狮城地标诗学》与《长夏之诗》
email_body:
陈志锐老师您好：

《狮城地标诗学》以诗写新加坡的地标，并获得新加坡文学奖华文诗歌组；2022年在台北出版的《长夏之诗》又把目光投向这座常夏之城。我也读到您白天在国立教育学院任教，夜里写作、练书法、作画。

想请教您：书法与绘画的经验，是否影响了您在诗中观看和描写城市地标的方式？

The Author Ledger 是一个独立项目，刊登简短的作者专访。专访通过几道书面问题完成，您可按自己的节奏作答；发表前，全文会先交给您审阅。

不知您是否愿意参与？无论如何都不必有压力。

此致敬礼，
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Landmark Poetics of the Lion City (2017) won SLP Chinese poetry; Poems of the Long Summer (Taipei 2022); NIE associate professor who also does calligraphy and painting (poetry.sg, Esplanade, Book Council via search results).
